correctness.rationale: Represent f up to a constant as the signed Df-integral of H_t. In the Hilbert direct sum of dyadic residuals the map t↦T H_t is continuous, also for infinite depth by the uniform squared-norm tail bound Σ 2^(−j)/4; thus the signed measure integral and the norm and Jensen bounds apply. At level j a single partially cut cell gives 2^(−j)φ(2^jt), where φ(u)={u}(1−{u}); this is zero at cell boundaries. Writing d=min({u},1−{u}), the two-level expression is 2d−3d²=1/3−3(d−1/3)². The exact paired geometric sum gives (4/9)(1−4^(−m)) for 2m levels and 4/9 in the limit. The first pair forces t=1/3 or 2/3, both fixed modulo 1 by multiplication by 4. For a general equality case, Jensen first forces support on those two sites; the two first-level centered jumps have Gram determinant s(1−t)(t−s)>0 for s<t, so the signed responses cannot be identical or collinear and both sites cannot carry positive variation mass in an equality case. Dropping all terms after the first pair gives the asserted variation-measure localization; only for single jumps is the full paired deficit an identity. Haar Parseval counts each kth detail k+1 times. No assertion for odd cutoffs; the frozen finite checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: A natural sharp multiscale BV approximation constant improves the naïve 1/2 obtained by separate level estimates. Exact equality picks a two-cycle rather than independently centered jumps at each level, and the exact deficits yield a useful quantitative necessary condition on near-extremal variation measures. The even cutoff is justified by the intrinsic two-scale pairing rather than an arbitrary truncation.
